name: wardrobe_nether_portal
source_title: Портал у шафі (Portal in a Wardrobe)

origin.description: Front-left-bottom corner of attachment-inclusive voxel bounding box; +X right, +Y up, +Z back; front faces north. Structural front-left-bottom is (1,0,1).

layer_format: layers[y][z][x]; rows run front to back, characters run left to right; every cell is explicit, including air

dimension_audit.explanation: The printed 4-block widths refer to the structural frame, not an overall bounding box including attachments. Open side trapdoors occupy x=0 and x=5; buttons occupy z=0. Central bottom slabs at y=6 end at height 6.5. No seventh full-height wall course is added.

assumptions: A single oblique photograph cannot determine every hidden state exactly. Printed dimensions and named materials take precedence; obscured trim, attachment states and symmetry are inferred rather than claimed to be independently visible.

The diagram labels oak trapdoors, so the 2x5 side panels and 4x2 lid use oak_trapdoor, despite their dark appearance in the print. Side panels are mirrored, closed against the exterior when open=true, and start one block above the base; the lid is bottom-half horizontal at y=6 over the six-high frames.

The two lower dark oak doors are shown open, with hinges at the outside edges. They occupy y=0 and y=1. Build on a solid level floor, which supplies their support and is intentionally not part of the schematic.

The small square-paneled fascia immediately above the open entrance is interpreted as two vertical dark oak trapdoors at y=2, not a third door half or an unsupported second pair of doors. Its exact hidden construction is not specified by a separate book callout.

The lower pedestal and projecting upper ledge use inverted dark oak stairs. The two central bottom slabs form the raised 6.5-high crest. Recessed upper paneling is represented by the visible dark oak plank face without extra filler rows.
Two dark oak buttons are placed on the lowest outer pedestal faces as handles; hidden extra handles are not invented.

Two plain white wall banners hang inward from the inner front-frame posts at y=4. The far-side banner is inferred by symmetry. Banner cloth extends below its anchor cell; no custom patterns or block-entity NBT are included.

The 2x4 portal interior remains air, not portal blocks, glass, water or lava. After construction ignite the obsidian opening manually. Adjacent air cells are intentional entrance and internal space; do not substitute structural blocks there.
No surrounding room, character, lights, decorative cobwebs, floor, entities, fluids or custom block-entity payloads are included.

spot_checks.note: Left base handle, faces front; pedestal supports it.
Left door lower half at floor level.
Left door upper half, matching hinge and facing.
Paneled fascia above the two-block door.
Left inward-facing white banner, backed by left post.
Bottom of left five-high side panel.
Top of right five-high side panel.
Central half-height crest ends at physical height 6.5.
No invented full-width top slab row.

build_notes: Paste/build at the attachment-inclusive origin on solid level ground; front is north. The actual door cells begin at local (2,0,1) and (3,0,1).
Expected non-air block-state cells: 90. Door halves count as four cells but require two door items. Wall banners count as two anchor cells.
Ignite the obsidian interior at local (2,1,3) with flint and steel after the bot finishes. No automatic portal activation is encoded.
